bio: Heritage farm island off Phillip Island with historic grounds, daily farming activities and free walking trails.
Phillip Island's highest point, with 4 to 8 km cliff walks above a surf beach and a Pinnacles return from the sand.
Racing circuit with a viewing mound showing most of the track and a display on the island's racing since 1928.
gaps: Track tours not found on the official site; viewing availability depends on circuit hire.

bio: Newhaven museum on Australia's role in the Vietnam War, with galleries on veterans' experiences and a Garden of Reflection.
Mangrove and saltmarsh boardwalks on the north shore, plus a 500 m walk up an observation tower over Western Port.
Newhaven chocolate maker with a free shop and cafe and a ticketed interactive tour past a chocolate waterfall.
Family park with a giant 3D maze, 19-hole mini golf and a 10 m high ropes course, indoors and out.
Western Port island reached by passenger ferry, with a national park holding Victoria's most significant koala population.
gaps: Parks Victoria 'area is closed' banner not verified as a real closure; ferries can be cancelled at short notice.

bio: Wonthaggi's former state coal mine, worked 1910 to 1968, with guided underground tours daily at 11.30am and 2pm.
gaps: Page carries a closed banner and works are underway; check status before relying on tours.

bio: Junction Park lookout at Wentworth, about 20 km west of Mildura, where the Darling River meets the Murray.
Semi-arid botanic garden at Buronga with Australian arid plants and a rose garden of over 1,600 bushes, free to enter.
Riverside park on the Murray at Mildura with a large sandbar beach for swimming, occasionally lifeguard-patrolled.
Historic river port with daily paddlesteamer departures, the PS Adelaide at the wharf and a Discovery Centre with a sawmill.
Murray floodplain park with forest trails, canoeing and Aboriginal oven mounds along the Lakes Loop Track.
gaps: Some tracks may be closed by flooding; check before travel.

bio: Yorta Yorta cultural hub in Barmah National Park, with a 1.2 km interpretive trail loop and Murray river cruises.
gaps: Centre is being renewed and Parks Victoria flags closure notices; current status unverified.

bio: Zoos Victoria wildlife park at Kyabram in the Goulburn Valley, with native animals and walking trails.
gaps: Animal numbers and keeper talks came from a snippet that may quote another park, so they are left out; confirm against the Kyabram page.

bio: Park of granite outcrops, woodland and grasslands, with a short steep climb to views from Mt Terrick Terrick.
Remote mallee park in Victoria's north-west with bush camping, birdwatching, hiking and 4WD tracks.
gaps: Largest-in-Victoria claim not in facts, so omitted.

bio: Salt lakes in Murray-Sunset National Park that turn pink in late summer, once the site of a salt industry until 1975.
Murray River park near Mildura with a chain of lakes, the Lake Mournpall Walk and Warepil Lookout Tower.
gaps: Floodplain restoration works June to December 2026 bring temporary track closures in the northern park.

bio: Semi-arid park in the north-west with a chain of lake beds linked by Outlet Creek and a sealed road to Wonga camping.
Victoria's largest salt lake, 6 km north of Sea Lake, where in dry periods you can walk onto the salt crust.
9,330 ha park beside the Murray between Echuca and Koondrook, with bend camping areas and four wheel driving.
gaps: Rainfall and watering are affecting access; some track closures.

bio: Open-air museum at Swan Hill, opened in 1966, with a one-hour Pyap River Cruise on the paddle steamer Gem.
